classification.difficultyReason: Justify the same angle through two explicitly requested routes: equal-leg tangent ratios and equal base angles combined with the triangle angle sum.

content.prompt:
Toby constructed two isosceles right triangles.
He says that when the two short sides are the same the angle $\theta$ is always $45^\circ$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show he is correct, using trigonometry in the two triangles.

spec.description: Equal perpendicular legs, Roman numeral I, and the acute theta at the bottom right.
spec.mathematics: Both legs are 12 cm; bottom-left angle is right.
spec.answerVisibility: The unknown angle is not evaluated.

spec.description: Second equal-leg triangle, positioned to the right of I for comparison.
spec.mathematics: Both legs are 17 cm; bottom-left angle is right.
spec.answerVisibility: The unknown angle is not evaluated.

answer.worked:
Triangle I:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{12}{12}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}(1)\\\theta&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
Triangle II:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{17}{17}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}(1)\\\theta&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
Both triangles have $\theta=45^\circ$, so Toby is correct.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show he is correct, using properties of isosceles triangles and angle sum of a triangle.

answer.short: The two acute angles are equal. $2\theta+90^\circ=180^\circ$, so $\theta=45^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The angles opposite the equal sides are equal, so both acute angles are $\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta+\theta+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\theta&=90^\circ\\\theta&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
